$comment: Parts of this repository that exist only for the starter's own public instance (starter.flooper.me) and its repository. `bun run starter:strip` removes them from a project made from the template (docs/guides/how-to-start-a-project.md). A new starter-only part is added here in the same PR (docs/processes/development.md#starter-only-parts); test/architecture/starter-only.test.ts checks every path, setting, job and patch, and the CI job starter-strip applies the default set to a scratch copy and runs typecheck, lint and test.

components.title: Automated QA of the starter's production
components.why: The starter tests its own deployment at starter.flooper.me with real accounts and no human: a QA suite with its journeys (apps/web/test/qa, #53, #54), a QA workflow with a GitHub environment, and in the app the QA bypass of Turnstile, the QA outbox that keeps QA mail instead of sending it, the QA admin and the /api/qa endpoints (#59). A new project has none of that: the strip deletes all of it, its settings, its rate-limit binding, its cron entry, audit events and tests, and regenerates 0000_init without the qa_outbox table. Keep it with --keep qa-automation to run the automated QA against your own deployment.

docs.heading: How to QA a deployment
docs.content:
# How to QA a deployment

The checks of a deployed environment. Use when you release to production or staging, or after a change to auth, email, workspaces, billing, notifications, storage, privacy or the admin portal.

| Layer            | What                                                                       | Run                                                          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Browser journeys | Every critical journey against a local dev server                          | `bun run test:e2e`, in CI on every pull request              |
| Production smoke | Pages, redirects, endpoints, headers, accessibility, signed out, read-only | `bun run test:smoke -- --env production`, after every deploy |
| Checklist        | Every feature with real accounts and real mail, by hand                    | [the checklist](#the-checklist) below, after a release       |

docs.heading: The automated suite
docs.content:
## The checklist

Walk each feature on the deployment as a person would, with an account at a mailbox you can read and a second account (B) in a separate browser profile. For each: do it, check the result and the mail it sends, and record pass, fail (with the screenshot and the reference shown in the error) or N/A. For every mail: it arrived, the sender is the environment's `EMAIL_FROM`, links point at the environment's origin, and notifications carry `List-Unsubscribe`.

| Feature                                         | Guide                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sign-up, verification, sign-in, password reset  | [how-to-setup-auth.md](how-to-setup-auth.md), [how-to-setup-email.md](how-to-setup-email.md)                                       |
| Bot check and rate limits                       | [how-to-configure-abuse-protection.md](how-to-configure-abuse-protection.md)                                                       |
| Two-factor and passkeys                         | [how-to-configure-account-security.md](how-to-configure-account-security.md)                                                       |
| Workspaces, invitations and roles               | [how-to-configure-workspaces.md](how-to-configure-workspaces.md)                                                                   |
| Settings                                        | [how-to-use-settings.md](how-to-use-settings.md)                                                                                   |
| Files                                           | [how-to-setup-r2.md](how-to-setup-r2.md)                                                                                           |
| Billing                                         | [how-to-configure-plans-and-billing.md](how-to-configure-plans-and-billing.md)                                                     |
| Notifications                                   | [how-to-send-notifications.md](how-to-send-notifications.md)                                                                       |
| Trash                                           | [how-to-use-trash.md](how-to-use-trash.md)                                                                                         |
| Privacy: export and delete                      | [how-to-handle-data-privacy.md](how-to-handle-data-privacy.md)                                                                     |
| Audit log                                       | [how-to-use-the-audit-log.md](how-to-use-the-audit-log.md)                                                                         |
| Admin portal and feature flags                  | [how-to-use-admin-portal.md](how-to-use-admin-portal.md), [how-to-use-feature-flags.md](how-to-use-feature-flags.md)               |
| Agents: connect Claude, call a tool, disconnect | [how-to-setup-mcp.md](how-to-setup-mcp.md)                                                                                         |
| Your features, the command palette              | [how-to-add-a-feature.md](how-to-add-a-feature.md)                                                                                 |
| Background jobs and email                       | [how-to-add-background-jobs.md](how-to-add-background-jobs.md)                                                                     |
| Landing, docs and search                        | [how-to-publish-docs-and-landing.md](how-to-publish-docs-and-landing.md), [how-to-define-branding.md](how-to-define-branding.md)   |
| Health and security headers                     | [how-to-monitor-health.md](how-to-monitor-health.md), [how-to-configure-security-headers.md](how-to-configure-security-headers.md) |
| Public demo, if you turn it on                  | [how-to-run-a-public-demo.md](how-to-run-a-public-demo.md)                                                                         |

Finish by deleting the accounts you created (Settings › Privacy › **Delete account**), never with SQL.

components.title: The starter's production instance config
components.why: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc and the deploy script carry the values of starter.flooper.me: its custom domain, D1 database id, Turnstile widget, sender, bootstrap admin and the starter owner's choices of workspace mode, sign-up, billing, two-factor and analytics. A project gets its own from the setup scripts; this resets them so nothing deploys onto the starter's resources by accident.

wrangler.comment:
Served only on its custom domain: replace app.example.com with the project's hostname
(the zone must be in this account; docs/guides/how-to-setup-web-app.md#deploy). The
APP_URL secret of this environment is https:// plus that hostname.
Test key: replace with the production widget's site key (bun run doctor warns).

json.value: CLOUDFLARE_ENV=production SITE_URL=https://app.example.com bun run build && wrangler deploy

docs.note: examples name starter.flooper.me; they are examples, replace them with your hostname when you like

manual: Set the production hostname: routes in env.production of apps/web/wrangler.jsonc (now app.example.com) and SITE_URL in the deploy:production script of apps/web/package.json.

Give the project its own resources and rate-limit namespace block: bun run setup:cloudflare --env all --dry-run, then without --dry-run (it writes the D1 ids and the namespace_ids; bun run doctor fails until then).
Choose the product settings per environment: bun run setup:auth --env <env> (a deploy refuses to start until you have), bun run setup:analytics --env <env>, bun run setup:storage.
Pick the sender per environment: bun run setup:email --env <env>; create the Turnstile widgets and put their site keys in the vars (bun run setup:cloudflare prints how).

docs.heading: Cloudflare Starter
docs.content:
# {{name}}

Built from the [Cloudflare starter](https://github.com/flooper68/cloudflare-starter): one Astro web Worker that serves the site, a Better Auth–protected React SPA, the API, a queue consumer and Cron Triggers, plus a shared feature package and a component library. Describe the product here.

docs.content:
## Starting from the starter

How this project was made from the template, what was stripped and what to keep or replace: [docs/guides/how-to-start-a-project.md](docs/guides/how-to-start-a-project.md).

Decide what /docs becomes: keep publishing the repository's docs, point DOCS.sources at product docs, or remove it (same guide).

components.title: Home page v2
components.why: The landing page (#56) markets the starter: its hero scene, the feature map and pillars from one feature data module (apps/web/src/landing/content.ts), the What's new strip and the footer. A product replaces it with its own; the strip does not write a landing page for you, it prints the steps.
manual: Replace the home page with the product's: the copy and feature data in apps/web/src/landing/content.ts, the sections of apps/web/src/pages/index.astro and its components (HeroScene.astro, FeatureMap.astro), and apps/web/test/e2e-build/landing.spec.ts with them (docs/reference/docs-site.md#replace-the-landing-page).

components.title: The starter's walkthrough videos
components.why: The recorded videos show the starter itself (its tour, Agents & MCP, the home page's loops): their scripts, catalogue entries and manifest entries; the docs' ::video directives stay and show their posters. A project records videos of its own product, or none. The pipeline stays: the recorder, the seed's structure, the upload, the /media route, the player and the workflow.
manual: The starter's videos are in R2 under media/<hash>/ of each environment's FILES bucket you uploaded them to; delete that prefix if you did (wrangler r2 object delete, or the dashboard).

To show your product's own videos, write scripts for them and record (docs/guides/how-to-record-walkthrough-videos.md#write-a-video-script); change the seed in apps/web/media/lib/seed.ts to your product's sample data.

components.title: The name Cloudflare Starter
components.why: The app calls itself Cloudflare Starter in page titles, mails, the authenticator issuer, the passkey name, the MCP server and the docs site. Replaced by the project's name (--name); the brand's mark, colours and fonts are a design step (docs/guides/how-to-define-branding.md).
manual: Give the project its own brand: name, tagline, mark, accent, fonts and radius in packages/ui/src/brand/ (docs/guides/how-to-define-branding.md). The short name Starter is brand.name there.

Rename the cloudflare-starter-* resources in apps/web/wrangler.jsonc (Worker, databases, buckets, queues, datasets) before setup:cloudflare creates them, and the @cloudflare-starter/* package scope if you like.

The upload demo stays: it is the only UI of the file storage feature (strip it with file storage, README › Strip what the product does not use).

### Background jobs and email

Guides: [how-to-add-background-jobs.md](../../../../docs/guides/how-to-add-background-jobs.md), [how-to-setup-email.md](../../../../docs/guides/how-to-setup-email.md).

Expected: the job completes within a minute; the mail arrives.
